title: Solar Physics, Helioseismology and Space Weather in the Bounce Frame

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Annika Olsson, and this is Solar Physics, Helioseismology and Space Weather in the Bounce Frame. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Annika Olsson, and this is Solar Physics, Helioseismology and Space Weather in the Bounce Frame. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'The Acoustic Cut-off Frequency of the Solar Atmosphere from Scale Height and Sound Speed, and the Reflection of Five-Minute Oscillations'. Its stated result: The paper computes its solar quantity from published observations and compares it with the torsion bounce frame's fixed scales (bound density 9.72e+54 g/cm3; solar central density at a fraction 1.54e-53 of that bound). Headline computed values: nu ac photosphere mHz = 4.64; nu ac chromosphere mHz = 3.98; five min freq mHz = 3.33; ratio 5min to cutoff = 0.718; period at cutoff min = 3.59.
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Solar Angular Momentum and Wind Braking: The Present Spin-Down Torque and the Braking Timescale It Implies'. Its stated result: The paper computes its solar quantity from published observations and compares it with the torsion bounce frame's fixed scales (bound density 9.72e+54 g/cm3; solar central density at a fraction 1.54e-53 of that bound). Headline computed values: J kg m2 s = 1.540e+41; rotational energy J = 2.080e+35; torque N m = 1.854e+23; braking time Gyr = 26.3; fraction lost per Gyr = 0.038.
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Coronal Mass Ejection Kinetic Energies: Observed Speeds, Masses and the Gravitational and Magnetic Ceilings Above Them'. Its stated result: The paper computes its solar quantity from published observations and compares it with the torsion bounce frame's fixed scales (bound density 9.72e+54 g/cm3; solar central density at a fraction 1.54e-53 of that bound). Headline computed values: max KE J = 2.000e+26; escape speed km s = 618; max KE fraction Lsun hour = 1.451e-04.
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'From Solar Wind Ram Pressure to Magnetopause Standoff: Quiet Conditions, a Fast Ejection, and the Storm-Time Energy Input at Earth'. Its stated result: The paper computes its solar quantity from published observations and compares it with the torsion bounce frame's fixed scales (bound density 9.72e+54 g/cm3; solar central density at a fraction 1.54e-53 of that bound). Headline computed values: P quiet nPa = 1.34; P storm nPa = 83.6; ratio pressures = 62.5; standoff quiet Re = 10.2; standoff storm Re = 5.13; standoff ratio = 0.502.
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Depth, Temperature and Convective Flux at the Base of the Solar Convection Zone Compared with the Frame's Energy Bounds'. Its stated result: The paper computes its solar quantity from published observations and compares it with the torsion bounce frame's fixed scales (bound density 9.72e+54 g/cm3; solar central density at a fraction 1.54e-53 of that bound). Headline computed values: r cz Rsun = 0.713; depth km = 1.997e+05; T cz K = 2.300e+06; flux W m2 = 1.238e+08; P gas Pa = 6.225e+12; P rad Pa = 7.057e+09.
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'The Solar Core Margin: Central Density and Temperature Set Against the Bounce Density and Temperature Ceiling'. Its stated result: The paper computes its solar quantity from published observations and compares it with the torsion bounce frame's fixed scales (bound density 9.72e+54 g/cm3; solar central density at a fraction 1.54e-53 of that bound). Headline computed values: rho c g cm3 = 150; T c K = 1.570e+07; ratio rho = 1.544e-53; T ceiling K = 3.278e+22; ratio T = 4.790e-16; rad energy density J m3 = 4.597e+13.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “The Acoustic Cut-off Frequency of the Solar Atmosphere from Scale Height and Sound Speed, and the Reflection of Five-Minute Oscillations”. Its stated result is: The paper computes its solar quantity from published observations and compares it with the torsion bounce frame's fixed scales (bound density 9.72e+54 g/cm3; solar central density at a fraction 1.54e-53 of that bound). (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'The Acoustic Cut-off Frequency of the Solar Atmosphere from Scale Height and Sound Speed, and the Reflection of Five-Minute Oscillations'; 'Solar Angular Momentum and Wind Braking: The Present Spin-Down Torque and the Braking Timescale It Implies'; 'Coronal Mass Ejection Kinetic Energies: Observed Speeds, Masses and the Gravitational and Magnetic Ceilings Above Them'; 'From Solar Wind Ram Pressure to Magnetopause Standoff: Quiet Conditions, a Fast Ejection, and the Storm-Time Energy Input at Earth'; 'Depth, Temperature and Convective Flux at the Base of the Solar Convection Zone Compared with the Frame's Energy Bounds'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

questions.teach: Think back to the lesson — the paper 'The Acoustic Cut-off Frequency of the Solar Atmosphere from Scale Height and Sound Speed, and the Reflection of Five-Minute Oscillations'. The result it reported gives a value for nu ac photosphere mHz, and that value is what this question asks for.
questions.teach2: Here is the exact passage from the lesson again: 'The Acoustic Cut-off Frequency of the Solar Atmosphere from Scale Height and Sound Speed, and the Reflection of Five-Minute Oscillations'. Its stated result: The paper computes its solar quantity from published observations and compares it with the torsion bounce frame's fixed scales (bound density 9.72e+54 g/cm3; solar central density at a fraction 1.54e-53 of that bound). Headline computed values: nu ac photosphere mHz = 4.64; nu ac chromosphere mHz = 3.98; five min freq mHz = 3.33; ratio 5min to cutoff = 0.718; period at cutoff min = 3.59. And here is that same result with the words stripped away — just the quantities standing in a row: nu ac photosphere mHz = 4.64; nu ac chromosphere mHz = 3.98; five min freq mHz = 3.33. Find nu ac photosphere mHz in that row; the value beside it is the one this question asks for. Say it in figures, any honest form: as printed, rounded, or written out in full.
questions.walk: Walk it through with me, step by step. (1) In the lesson, the paper 'The Acoustic Cut-off Frequency of the Solar Atmosphere from Scale Height and Sound Speed, and the Reflection of Five-Minute Oscillations' stated its result. (2) That result pairs names with values: nu ac photosphere mHz = 4.64; nu ac chromosphere mHz = 3.98; five min freq mHz = 3.33. (3) This question asks for the value paired with nu ac photosphere mHz. (4) In that row, nu ac photosphere mHz stands beside 4.64 — so the answer the lesson gives is 4.64. Now it is yours: say that value, in any honest form.
questions.q: In the lesson, the paper 'The Acoustic Cut-off Frequency of the Solar Atmosphere from Scale Height and Sound Speed, and the Reflection of Five-Minute Oscillations' reported a number for nu ac photosphere mHz. What number did it report?
questions.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
